title: Deferred Theoretical & Clinical Questions Archive
description: Archived questions that test theoretical concepts, drug indications, mechanisms of action, regulatory history, or general pharmaceutical knowledge. These questions are intentionally removed from active beginner/intermediate LASA learning sessions and preserved here for future thesis clinical simulation and comprehensive assessment phases.
scopePolicy: Active Duoclongo learning content strictly prioritizes: Tall Man Lettering construction, LASA drug identification, LASA drug distinction, and realistic situational LASA recognition. Theoretical and clinical decision-making content is deferred until formal thesis research and validation phases.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Tests pharmacological classification and drug indication knowledge ('analgesic' vs 'glaucoma agent') rather than direct name recognition/distinction.
archivedQuestions.prompt: Which of the following represents a documented LASA hazard between an analgesic and a glaucoma agent?
choices: acetaminophen / acetaZOLAMIDE
Abelcet / amphotericin B
Accupril / Aciphex
Actonel / Actos
archivedQuestions.explanation: Acetaminophen (analgesic/antipyretic) and acetaZOLAMIDE (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor for glaucoma) share substantial phonetic and visual prefixes.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Tests passive memorization of whether ISMP recognizes a pair rather than testing active orthographic discrimination.
archivedQuestions.prompt: acetaZOLAMIDE and acetoHEXAMIDE are recognized by ISMP as a Look-Alike, Sound-Alike pair.
choices: True
False
archivedQuestions.explanation: Both acetaZOLAMIDE and acetoHEXAMIDE share identical prefixes ('acet-') and endings ('-amide'), creating severe dispensing confusion.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Tests abstract medication safety definitions and risk factor theory rather than medication name distinction.
archivedQuestions.prompt: In the LASA pair Accupril and Aciphex, what is the primary risk factor for medication errors?
choices: Phonetic sound-alike and visual look-alike brand names
Identical dosage forms and tablet colors
Identical active pharmaceutical ingredients
Same clinical indications for hypertension
archivedQuestions.correctAnswer: Phonetic sound-alike and visual look-alike brand names
archivedQuestions.explanation: Accupril and Aciphex possess strong phonemic and orthographic similarity despite differing in therapeutic class.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Tests pharmacological release kinetics theory (immediate-release vs extended-release pharmacodynamics) rather than label distinction.
archivedQuestions.prompt: Adderall is commonly confused with Adderall XR when release mechanisms are overlooked. What is the primary clinical difference?
choices: Adderall is immediate-release while Adderall XR is extended-release
Adderall is a prodrug while Adderall XR is an active metabolite
Adderall contains dextroamphetamine only while XR contains lisdexamfetamine
Adderall is sublingual while Adderall XR is swallowed whole
archivedQuestions.correctAnswer: Adderall is immediate-release while Adderall XR is extended-release
archivedQuestions.explanation: Adderall provides rapid, immediate release requiring multi-dose daily scheduling, whereas Adderall XR delivers biphasic extended release over 10-12 hours.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Tests clinical pathophysiology (severe hypoglycemia in non-diabetic patients) rather than medication name identification.
archivedQuestions.prompt: What is the primary clinical risk if acetoHEXAMIDE is accidentally dispensed instead of acetaZOLAMIDE?
choices: Severe drug-induced hypoglycemia in a non-diabetic patient
Sudden elevation of intraocular pressure causing optic nerve damage
Hypertensive crisis from unmonitored alpha-agonist stimulation
Acute renal tubular acidosis from carbonic anhydrase overstimulation
archivedQuestions.correctAnswer: Severe drug-induced hypoglycemia in a non-diabetic patient
archivedQuestions.explanation: AcetoHEXAMIDE is a first-generation sulfonylurea that stimulates pancreatic insulin secretion. Inadvertently dispensing it causes profound hypoglycemia.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Tests therapeutic indications (osteoporosis bisphosphonate vs type 2 diabetes thiazolidinedione) rather than LASA name distinction.
archivedQuestions.prompt: Actonel (risedronate) is dangerously confused with Actos (pioglitazone). What is the primary indication of Actonel?
choices: Osteoporosis (bisphosphonate)
Type 2 diabetes (thiazolidinedione)
Acute myocardial infarction (thrombolytic)
Severe hypercholesterolemia (statin)
archivedQuestions.explanation: Actonel is a bisphosphonate for osteoporosis, while Actos is an oral antidiabetic for type 2 diabetes.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Tests clinical vaccine population theory (pediatric vs adolescent/adult antigen concentrations) rather than name distinction.
archivedQuestions.prompt: Which population is Adacel (Tdap) specifically formulated for, compared to pediatric Daptacel (DTaP)?
choices: Adolescents and adults (booster with reduced toxoid)
Infants under 6 weeks of age exclusively
Pregnant patients in their first trimester only
Geriatric patients with renal insufficiency
archivedQuestions.correctAnswer: Adolescents and adults (booster with reduced toxoid)
archivedQuestions.explanation: Adacel (Tdap, lowercase 'd' and 'p') has lower diphtheria and pertussis antigen content meant as a booster for ages 10-64.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Tests regulatory naming history and antibody-drug conjugate dosing mechanism theory rather than name discrimination.
archivedQuestions.prompt: Why did the FDA and ISMP require the 'ado-' prefix for ado-trastuzumab emtansine (Kadcyla)?
choices: To prevent fatal dosing mix-ups with conventional trastuzumab (Herceptin)
To signify that it can be administered via intramuscular injection
To denote that it is an oral biosimilar version of Herceptin
To allow pharmacists to substitute it automatically without a new prescription
archivedQuestions.correctAnswer: To prevent fatal dosing mix-ups with conventional trastuzumab (Herceptin)
archivedQuestions.explanation: Ado-trastuzumab emtansine is an antibody-drug conjugate with cytotoxic emtansine. Confusing it with conventional trastuzumab causes life-threatening overdoses.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Tests drug indications and pharmacological class (cholesterol management vs asthma inhaler) rather than medication name distinction.
archivedQuestions.prompt: Advair (fluticasone/salmeterol) is an inhaler for asthma. What is Advicor (niacin/lovastatin) indicated for?
choices: Lipid and cholesterol management
Severe hypertension and congestive heart failure
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation
Type 2 diabetes glycemic control
archivedQuestions.explanation: Advicor is an oral combination of niacin and lovastatin for hyperlipidemia, whereas Advair is an inhaled steroid/bronchodilator combination for respiratory disease.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Tests high-alert ISMP classification theory and respiratory depression mechanisms rather than distinguishing confusable opioid medication names.
archivedQuestions.prompt: Why are fentaNYL and ALfentanil designated as high-alert LASA medications by ISMP?
choices: They have dramatically different potencies and rapid onset, where dosing confusion causes fatal respiratory depression
They are non-controlled analgesics that require refrigeration to prevent degradation
They share identical generic chemical structures and are legally interchangeable
They are administered only via topical creams that cause contact dermatitis
archivedQuestions.correctAnswer: They have dramatically different potencies and rapid onset, where dosing confusion causes fatal respiratory depression
archivedQuestions.explanation: Fentanyl is roughly 10-20 times more potent than alfentanil. Confusing the names leads to catastrophic opioid overdose and respiratory failure.

archivedQuestions.deferredReason: Passive true/false query about ISMP rules replaced with active orthographic Tall Man distinction task.
archivedQuestions.prompt: In the ISMP Tall Man lettering standard, fentaNYL capitalizes the suffix NYL while ALfentanil capitalizes the prefix AL.
choices: True
False
archivedQuestions.explanation: ISMP differentiates fentaNYL (suffix capitalized) from ALfentanil and SUFentanil (prefixes capitalized) to prevent look-alike opioid catastrophes.
